messages:
marie: starting a bring-up for kythera9b-int4 on dedicated. quick smoke: coherent for the first ~90-120 tokens, then model starts repeating phrases and punctuation spacing gets odd. ppl delta ~+11.3 vs fp16 on our long-prompts set.
sandeep: can you paste a tiny excerpt of diff?
marie: sample diff: `fp16: "He said — and paused."` vs `int4: "He said - - and paused ."` 
marie: attaching full diff to the issue but the pattern looks like both rotary degradation + tokenizer id drift.
jordan: kythera uses per-head rotary scale (headwise) and a nonstandard rotary base frequency. conversion tools sometimes collapse headwise params into a single float which will change attention dynamics for long contexts.
alex: also saw that kythera bumped a cluster of rare tokens into the high 50k range in the tokenizer.json recently. if token ids shift by a constant during export/conversion the kv cache index math `kv_pos = token_id - base_token` can silently break and manifest as later-context hallucinations.
marie: i re-ran `convert.py` with `--preserve-metadata` but our older convert still defaults to `rotary_mode: global` when it can't find head metadata.
sandeep: try forcing headwise on a local load: i ran inference with a runtime override `--rotary-mode=headwise --rotary-head-scale=1.15` and the int4 traces aligned much more with fp16 until ~800 tokens. without override it diverged by ~150 tokens.
jordan: that matches my hypothesis. two action items: make converter write explicit rotary metadata into model.json, and add a tokenizer.normalize field (nfc|nfkc|none) to tokenizer.json so encoders match.
ben: i'll take the quant sweep (AWQ/GPTQ) across scale/clip/grid with and without the headwise flag. can you put a tiny harness that toggles both tokenizer and rotary behaviour?
marie: pushed `tests/kythera/smoke_toggle.py` to the model-tools repo. usage: `python smoke_toggle.py --model kythera_int4 --rotary=headwise|global --token-norm=nfc|nfkc --seed 0` — it records ppl, repetitiveness score, and a token-id parity diff.
alex: FYI the tokenizer parity failure looks like this: `encode('–') -> fp16: [345, 678] | int4: [821, 678]`  the en-dash ended up as a different first subtoken. normalization mismatch.
marie: added unit tests to assert `encode/decode` parity between source and converted tokenizers for a 200-sample unicode set. failing tests currently show 13 mismatches.
sandeep: converter should also emit a `compatibility_report.json` alongside the converted model when it detects any of: missing rotary head metadata, tokenizer normalization mismatch, or token id reassignments > 2 tokens. that way downstream runtimes can decide to fail fast or use a recommended fallback.
jordan: agree. propose fields: `rotary_mode`, `rotary_head_scale`, `tokenizer_normalization`, `token_map_changes` (list of changed token ids). converters: log WARN and attach the report artifact.
ben: :thumbsup: once PR lands i'll run the matrix on redwood-dedicated pools and produce a summary table — ppl, rouge/bleu-ish proxies, and a repeat-rate metric. will tag the commits with matrix run ids.
ci-bot: job/kythera-int4-compat-sweep queued on redwood-dedicated-5 (job id kj-9944)
marie: small UX note: for `rotary_head_scale` we should store the per-head vector as a base64-encoded list if it's not a scalar, since some models use per-head small adjustments. converters should not flatten arrays -> scalar silently.
alex: +1 on base64 array. also add a `converter_version` and `source_ckpt_sha` into model.json so we can trace provenance.
sandeep: if the compatibility_report recommends fp16 fallback we should make the CLI `redwood-deploy` exit with non-zero unless `--force` is provided. safer for prod.
jordan: i'll sketch the converter PR: files `convert/patch_metadata.py`, unit tests in `tests/convert/test_metadata.py`, and a docs note about normalization choices.
marie: timeline: i'll open a draft PR today. ben will run the matrix after merge and we'll block Dedicated release until parity thresholds are met.
ben: i'll watch the PR and queue runs. ping me for infra keys.
marie: thanks all. I'll include a couple of representative token parity diffs in the PR and example runtime flags for backwards compatibility.
alex: 🙏
